situation: The government should spend less on the military and more on social welfare.
text: As a woman, I think social welfare by its very definition is to the benefit of society.  In contrast military spending is an expense that is necessary to counter weaknesses in society (and between nations).  As a fundamental rule, it is therefore always better to spend on social welfare, rather than the military.   However, having said that, there are good reasons to adequately fund the military to provide a level of insurance for the continued existence of society in its current form, given an uncertain global environment. I believe that there are so many out there born into disadvantaged environments who have incredible potential, yet they never explore this potential because they are given everything they need to get by within that environment. We shouldn't be handing out free meals; we should be supporting people to support themselves, and their future families, so that future generations are born into stronger environments and we can break this cycle.

The 'nation state' was linked in the past to a dominant ethnic group, particularly for the new nations created after the first world war and led to terrible treatment of minorities. Saying that, I think people should be proud of aspects of British culture and our historic achievements, but also be clear eyed about the dark aspects of our past. I'd like to see people taking more pride in their local areas and their communities, but that is at a smaller scale than the nation as a whole. In summary, i think to tackle the problems of the 21st century, we may need to think beyond the nation to an international scale. A daunting prospect going beyond anything we've managed before.

Student debt is not attractive to many, and certainly not a necessity should they be able to learn a trade and continue their education through employment. situation: It is wrong to pay people different wages for doing the same work.
text:
As a woman, I think yes massively so. If people are the same work, they should be paid the same. Anything else amounts to discrimination. The only exception to this i can think of is there is a bonus payment, which has a 'years in service' element to it. 

Race, gender or anything else should not influence the amount someone is paid. If someone is performing worse than someone else there should be performance review checkpoints which aim to work with the employee to improve performance. Of course if performance remains low, redundancy is fair option if undertaken in the correct manner.

I have had situations where people in the same team are paid wildly different salaries, sometimes even more than their managers. Once this information became public it became a very difficult situation for senior management, leading to a number of pay 'corrections' and people leaving the organisation to find better paying positions.

It is not legal for someone to change sex under the age of 18 so I dont understand why we would want to teach them about something that they are unable to do yet. This differs from teaching children the pitfalls of abusing alcohol or drugs as this serves as a stark warning. There is nothing to be afraid of around gender fluidity so this doesnt serve the same purpose, instead promotes this. I feel then that certain misconceptions then develop at a young age.
